Sports.title: Emotional Cristiano Ronaldo breaks down in tears as anonymous superstar sees World Cup dream crushed by Spain - with Arsenal star scoring late to shatter Portugal hearts
Sports.content:
Emotional Cristiano Ronaldo breaks down in tears as anonymous superstar sees World Cup dream crushed by Spain - with Arsenal star scoring late to shatter Portugal hearts

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The World Cup's A-list attackers have been dominating the headlines this summer but it is the Spanish backline which is proving the most extraordinary.

Luis de la Fuente's water-tight La Roja outfit are into the quarter-final after edging out Iberian neighbors Portugal in a true chess match at Dallas Stadium, where substitute Mikel Merino netted the game's only goal in the first minute of stoppage time.

Spain's remarkable defense, which had only allowed three shots on target prior to Monday's game, is still yet to concede a goal after five games. They also march into the next round on a record run of six straight clean sheets at this famous tournament.

In a game of very few clear-cut opportunities, Cristiano Ronaldo left the World Cup stage for the last time on the most depressing of notes. Sporting greats rarely go out on a high, too often the result of them outstaying their welcome, and that proved the case here.

Portugal's faded force touched the ball just 19 times across just over 96 minutes, the fewest of any starting player by some distance. Mikel Oyarzabal, who had the second-fewest, registered 35 touches.

After Goncalo Ramos' dramatic winner against Croatia in the last 32, Portugal boss Roberto Martinez had an unenviable decision to make at the pinpoint of his attack: either unleash his fresher, more in-form striker - who was averaging a goal or assist every 37 minutes at World Cups heading into Monday's game - or stick with Portugal's captain, their national icon, for what could be one last rodeo in Texas.

Mikel Merino's last-gasp strike earned Spain a 1-0 win over Portugal in the World Cup last 16

Cristiano Ronaldo was left in tears at full time after his World Cup dream was ended for good

While the former option probably made most logical sense, he avoided the daunting task of having to tell Ronaldo he would not be starting his potential last ever World Cup match. The 41-year-old kept his place despite the pressure on Martinez to swap him out for Ramos, 25.

And in the end, it proved the wrong decision as Ronaldo went largely anonymous once more, all while Ramos was left on the bench, before Merino came up with the game-winning goal at the death.

Ronaldo's miserable ending

Prior to the second-half hydration break, Ronaldo had failed to get on the end of a menacing cross from Pedro Neto, the kind he would have swept home 10 years ago, before sending a feeble attempt at a volley straight into Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon's hands. He laughed to himself afterwards almost in embarrassment at the faded force he has become.

And when the two teams stopped for some fluids, Portugal's veteran captain was the only player who needed to sit down on a water cooler. You can hardly blame him at his age.

Ronaldo still looks the part despite now being a 41-year-old man. The remarkable physique and slick hair remain, yet as soon as he begins to move around on the pitch it quickly becomes evident that his previous powers are no longer there.

How Martinez can seriously justify leaving out Ramos, the hero of last week's dramatic victory over Croatia who has just been snapped up by AC Milan for $80million, to accommodate him is a mystery.

Ronaldo looked a shadow of his former self as he departed on the most miserable of lows

After leaving the new Milan star on the bench, Portugal desperately chased an unlikely leveler after Merino's winner, but it was too little too late and their World Cup campaign has come to a miserable end.

An emotional Ronaldo, who bids farewell to a competition that provides the only blotch on his illustrious CV after never even making it to the final, shed a few tears at full-time after his fate was sealed.

Chalk and cheese

Less than 24 hours after England and Mexico played out an all-time classic over in Mexico City, Portugal and Spain offered up a much less memorable 90-plus minutes here.

This was always going to be a tactical battle of attrition between two managers with a love for possession-based football, and it proved exactly that for the majority. Up until the first hydration break, both goalkeepers were only seriously tested once each.

Oyarzabal should have at least drawn a save out of Portugal keeper Diogo Costa in the eighth minute. The Real Sociedad striker has been in solid form this summer, scoring four in four before this last-32 clash, yet after being released through on goal by Dani Olmo with just Costa to beat he dragged his shot wide of the post.

Four minutes later, the once-great Ronaldo officially joined the party with one of his only involvements in an otherwise tame first half, producing a trademark stepover before firing an effort straight at Spain keeper Unai Simon.

It was by no means a classic at Dallas Stadium as the two teams played out a real chess match

The chess match became a slightly more adventurous one for a little while after the first hydration break. Portugal came closest to finding the opener in the 37th minute, when Joao Felix pulled a header back across goal and, after the ball deflected off Simon, Ronaldo forced the Spain shot-stopper into an acrobatic save when he tried to turn it home.

Shortly before half-time, Portugal defender Nuno Mendes rattled the woodwork with a long-range effort which Pedro Porro got a head to, the Tottenham right-back's vital intervention sending it crashing against the bar.

The second half opened in similar fashion to the first, with very few chances for either team before they paused to rehydrate at the domed, climate-controlled home of the Dallas Cowboys. That's how FIFA are still selling it, anyway.

However, up until Merino swept home the winner in stoppage time, this was a drab affair that will hardly be remembered for days to come, let alone years. Although La Roja will not care one bit.

History for Spain

When they made it to the 41st minute with their clean sheet intact, Spain set the record for most consecutive World Cup minutes without conceding a goal, surpassing a Switzerland team who shut out the opposition for 559 minutes across the 1994, 2006 and 2010 tournaments.

They then went even further by banking their sixth consecutive clean sheet, having also been held to a 0-0 draw by Morocco before crashing out of the 2022 World Cup on penalties. No team in history has ever managed that feat.

Spain have kept a record six consecutive clean sheets at the World Cup after another shutout

With Rodri sweeping up in front of the formidable Aymeric Laporte and Pau Cubarsi, and with Pedro Porro and Marc Cucurella patrolling the flanks, De la Fuente's defensive unit is impregnable right now.

Unai Simon, who is De la Fuente's preferred man in goal over Arsenal's David Raya and Barcelona's Joan Garcia, only had three saves to make here. It means in their five matches, Spain have only conceded six shots on goal.

For all of the attacking beauty at this summer's tournament, La Roja's defense is just as worthy of the plaudits.

Yamal's frustrating night

Many will point to his miles on the clock and age to explain Ronaldo's increasing lack of influence on the pitch. Yet down the other end, Spanish wonderkid Yamal, who only turns 19 next week, was equally quiet early on.

La Roja's most fearsome forward had a poor start and was uncharacteristically sloppy in possession, though his only real opening came directly after he gifted the ball to Bruno Fernandes inside Spain's half in the 16th minute.

When Spain won it back, Yamal soon hurtled towards the Portugal box down the other end, cut past a defender in the box and pulled the trigger, only to be denied by Costa. From the rebound, Alex Baena's curling effort forced a much more dramatic save.

Lamine Yamal did not have the most effective of games over on the right-hand side for Spain

Yamal was beginning to have more joy on the right of Luis de la Fuente's frontline as the second half continued. Paris St-Germain's Mendes, who had been doing well to stifle the teenage sensation, was forced off with an injury just before the hour mark and replaced by 32-year-old Nelson Semedo of Fenerbahce. Up against a man almost twice his age, a Yamal with more time and space suddenly looked a danger once again.

The Barcelona wonderkid was not needed for the all-important winner, nonetheless. Instead it was the combination of two substitutes, Ferran Torres and Merino, which booked Spain's place in the quarter-final.

Torres first received the ball from Rodri and turned, before releasing the Arsenal star into the box as Ruben Dias frantically raced out to close him down. Merino was free to run through and slip the ball past Costa, sparking euphoric scenes on the Spanish bench.

While the team got the job done against tough opposition, and kept yet another clean sheet, Yamal will hope to have a more effective outing in the quarterfinals after extending his scoreless run to three games.

Sports.title: Paraguay's World Cup shame: Kylian Mbappe calls out 'despicable' South American senator and accuses her of 'brazen racism' after extraordinary social media attack on France star
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe has accused a Paraguayan senator of 'brazen racism' and labelled her 'despicable' after she launched an extraordinary social media attack on the France star following her country's World Cup elimination.

The Real Madrid forward scored a decisive second-half penalty to earn France a narrow 1-0 victory over Paraguay in Philadelphia on Saturday, but the round of 16 clash was marred by shameful and dirty tactics used by the underdogs.

Going up against the tournament favourites, the Paraguayans used every trick in the book to try and provoke their opponents, repeatedly fouling, faking injury and trying to wind up Les Bleus with overly aggressive conduct.

And now, Paraguay's controversial World Cup exit has taken another extraordinary turn after senator Celeste Amarilla launched a vile attack on France's captain.

After Mbappe refused a handshake with Paraguayan goalkeeper Orlando Gill, she claimed: 'This brute hasn't even learned to write' before hurling racist insults at the superstar.

'You should've shown him the finger, Orlando Gill; I do it in the senate and nothing happens!!!'

France captain Kylian Mbappe has accused a Paraguayan senator of 'brazen racism'

Paraguay senator Celeste Amarilla launched an extraordinary social media attack on Mbappe

She also wrote in a separate post, that Mbappe was 'pretending hard to be French, resentful, newly rich, arrogant, and ugly.

'He was nervous and scared to death the whole match, like his entire team; they couldn't even score a goal, they won by a fluke...

'The only thing many of us demanded of the Albirroja is not to have slapped him open-handed after the match ended. And that's despite not being a soccer fan.'

Mbappe furiously responded to her astonishing tirade with his own statement on Monday, which read: 'Madame Celeste Amarilla, You are a despicable woman and unworthy of your position. You do not represent Paraguay, that country which has sweated passion and honor throughout the competition.

'Through your recklessness and your brazen racism, the entire world has already forgotten the journey and the historic effort that your players accomplished during this World Cup, making way for an incompetent woman who gives the worst possible image of her country.

'I will never allow people like her the freedom to spread their hatred and racism across the world.'

French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo also threw his support behind Mbappe and posted: 'The racist remarks by Paraguayan Senator Celeste Amarilla targeting Kylian Mbappe are criminal and reprehensible.

'They must be prosecuted here as elsewhere. The FFF is filing a report with the prosecutor's office for the purpose of judicial proceedings.

Mbappe labelled her 'despicable' in a furious statement as he responsed on social media

Paraguay's dirty tactics overshadowed France's 1-0 win in the round of 16 on Saturday

Mbappe and Co were able to keep their cool in the face of relentless provocation

'I offer my full support to our captain, to the players, and more generally to all the victims of such odious remarks. The players of the French national team represent France; it is our country that is insulted.'

Paraguay's dirty tactics included various incidents during the match, from scuffing up the penalty spot, elbowing Dayot Upamecano in the ribs, palming Jules Kounde's face, trying to get Michael Olise sent off with outrageous play-acting and somehow ending up without a single booking from Uzbekistani referee Ilgiz Tantashev.

After the tempestuous match, BBC pundit Joe Hart branded Paraguay's players 'an absolute disgrace', while French newspaper L'Equipe slapped Tantashev with a brutal 1/10 rating for failing to seize control of the occasion.

In a tense flashpoint of the match, goalkeeper Gill was left furious after Mbappe refused to shake his hands while celebrating in front of the French fans.

Gill reacted furiously, throwing the ball at Mbappe's back before he walked over to the centre circle, where another melee took place.

Speaking after the match, Gill fumed: 'Kylian Mbappe has p***ed me off. I stretched my hand to congratulate him, but he ignored me.

'This is football, if they're not used to this, what can we do? Paraguay is like that, it's a tough team.

'From the first moment we set out to make ourselves felt on the field, that if the ball gets through, the man doesn't.'

Speaking about the controversial encounter, Mbappe hailed his side and said they are prepared to win via any method at this World Cup.

'We knew what kind of game we were going to have. We showed that we were not just a team that knows how to play offensive football,' he said.

'They thought we'd come wearing tuxedos, doing great plays, one-twos and whatnot. It's their way of playing.'

Sports.title: Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh hints at ANOTHER late night for sports fans as he issues demand for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury to be held in early hours at Wembley
Sports.content:
Saudi boxing chief Turki Alalshikh hints at ANOTHER late night for sports fans as he issues demand for Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury to be held in early hours at Wembley

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Turki Alalshikh has revealed Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury will take place before the end of the year but admitted the venue has still not been decided, with Wembley Stadium dependent on one major condition.

Speaking in London on Monday, the Chairman of the General Entertainment Authority (GEA) confirmed his preference is to stage the long-awaited all-British heavyweight showdown in England.

However, he made it clear any deal hinges on being able to hold the fight late enough to maximise its global audience - particularly in the United States.

'We will have Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury this year,' Alalshikh said. 'We haven't chosen the place yet. It depends on whether England gives us everything we need. We want to stage the fight in England but we want to make sure the time zone suits the whole world - especially in America.

'If they allow us to have Wembley, late in the night, we want to do it there. So, right now, it's about the time, viewership and subscribers. We will talk with the majors.'

The comments suggest Wembley remains the preferred destination, but only if officials are willing to approve an unusually late start time that would allow the fight to air in prime time across the United States.

Turki Alalshikh has revealed Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury will take place before the end of the year but admitted the venue has still not been decided

However, Alalshikh (left) has confirmed his preference is to stage the long-awaited all-British heavyweight showdown in England

However, he made it clear any deal hinges on being able to hold the fight late enough to maximise its global audience - particularly in the United States

Such a move would almost certainly mean another late night for British sports fans, with the main event potentially taking place in the early hours of the morning to satisfy international broadcasters and maximise subscribers on Netflix.

However, under Brent Council's licensing conditions, major events are generally expected to finish by around 11pm, with organisers required to adhere to agreed dispersal plans to minimise disruption for local residents and transport networks.

Extending beyond those hours would likely require special approval from the local authority and could come with significant additional costs, including extra staffing, policing, stewarding and transport arrangements.

His Excellency Turki Alalshikh made the comments while speaking in London during the official inauguration of SELA International's headquarters.

The event was attended alongside His Royal Highness Prince Abdullah bin Khaled bin Sultan bin Abdulaziz, Saudi Arabia's Ambassador to the United Kingdom.

Joshua and Fury are expected to meet later this year, provided both come through their warm-up fights this summer, with boxing fans now waiting to discover whether the blockbuster clash will finally land at Wembley or elsewhere.

Sports.title: Arthur's Fery-tale continues! British wildcard wins AGAIN in five-set epic against Grigor Dimitrov to reach Wimbledon quarter finals - with underdog mouthing hilarious X-rated comment after stunning victory
Sports.content:
Twenty five years after Goran Ivanisevic became the first wildcard to win Wimbledon, Britain's Arthur Fery is three wins away from becoming the second.

Born in Paris, raised in Wimbledon, this cross-Channel Fery is chugging further and faster than anyone could have anticipated.

On his Centre Court debut, on the biggest day of his life he produced the best match of his life - and all with Roger Federer looking on from the Royal Box.

The 23-year-old beat Grigor Dimitrov 7-5, 3-6, 4-6, 6-4, 7-6 and, for the second match in a row, the 5ft 9in pocket rocket proved he could squeeze through the narrowest gap; wriggle out of the stickiest situation.

Having come from 4-1 down in both the fourth and fifth sets of his second-round win over Zizou Bergs, Fery, trailing Dimitrov two sets to one, twice recovered from a break in the fourth set.

The man who began the grass court season with two Tour-level wins in his life has forgotten how to lose.

ARTHUR FERY IS A WIMBLEDON QUARTER-FINALIST 🤩 pic.twitter.com/NlBQqgru8a — BBC Sport (@BBCSport) July 6, 2026

Arthur Fery appeared to mouth an expletive in shock after reaching Wimbledon quarter-finals

Fery takes the acclaim of Centre Court after dispatching of Grigor Dimitrov

He has played four tiebreaks this fortnight and won the lot, and here is one illustration of his priceless ability to bring his best in the most pregnant moments: across three hours and 55 minutes Fery struck seven aces - and two of those came within five minutes of each other in the deciding tiebreak.

'It's incredibly hard to describe what I have just felt on that tennis court,' he told the crowd afterwards, and as he continued his ability to form full sentences deserted him: 'First time on this court, against an absolute legend of the game…I grew up five minutes from here…we've got the greatest of all time watching…'

On another comeback: 'It's been the story of the tournament, I'm playing really well with my back against the wall.'

He will face Italian No 9 seed Flavio Cobolli in the quarter-finals on Wednesday.

Even to parochial eyes, there were compelling narratives on both sides of the court: the Ferytale and the fairytale, if you will.

This was the first time in Grand Slam history two wildcards had faced off in the fourth round or later. Fery's reason for being handed that golden ticket was obvious; in Dimitrov's case the story is a little darker.

Britain's Fery is three wins away from becoming the second wildcard winner at Wimbledon

The 23-year-old beat the wily Bulgarian Grigor Dimitrov 7-5, 3-6, 4-6, 6-4, 7-6

It was on this very same second Monday of Wimbledon last year, on this very same court, when Dimitrov tore a pectoral muscle when leading eventual champion Jannik Sinner by two sets to love.

Eleven months and two weeks of the subsequent time has been hellish for the Bulgarian as first the physical and then the mental pain threatened to end the 35-year-old's career.

Suffering from flashbacks and crippling uncertainty, he came into the grass season with a seasonal record of one win and 11 defeats - including seven in a row.

But a couple of wins apiece in Dublin and Mallorca sparked a flame and that has grown into an inferno at Wimbledon as his talent has blazed into light.

Dimitrov was known in his early career as Baby Fed, his flowing single-handed backhand and all-round style reminiscent of the great Swiss.

The man himself, Roger Federer, was there the night of the Sinner match, looking on in horror from the Royal Box as his friend limped from the court; and here both men had played five-set matches coming into this fourth round, Fery that act of escapology against Bergs, Dimitrov an absorbing tussle with Matteo Berrettini.

In theory, this was a match between the 114th (Fery) and the 146th best tennis players in the world - the quality of the spectacle told otherwise.

As the surfaces have homogenized over the past 20 years, men's tennis has largely become a baseline battle of power and endurance.

This was a throwback to old school grass-court tennis. These two can give the ball a wallop - Fery had a forehand clocked at over 100mph this fortnight - but they can wield the surgeon's knife as well as the butcher's cleaver.

Roger Federer was looking on from the Royal Box as Fery made his Centre Court debut

After a couple of shanks in the first couple of games Fery settled well. There has been a serenity about his play here that suggested he would not be discombobulated by the occasion.

At 5-5, having thus far won only two points on the Dimitrov serve, Fery broke to love, cracking a couple of backhands and then hammering a forehand return.

For all the aesthetic beauty of the Dimitrov backhand - whether sliced or driven - it is his weaker side and Fery directed the majority of his fire in that direction.

Off his own backhand wing, Fery was simply not missing. Incredibly, he got through a set and seven games with one single unforced error on that side - and then it all fell apart, as he made three unforced errors in a row to concede the break at 3-4 in the second set.

Fery headed off-court for an eight-minute loo break - sadly standard practice these days. Of course, if you gotta go you gotta go but if it was more of an attempt to recentre himself, there is always the possibility you go further off-kilter.

And, upon his return to Centre Court, Fery played a second ragged service game in a row. The quality of the Brit backhand in the first period of the match meant Dimitrov was largely forced to employ his delightful but less offensive slice.

As Fery's level dipped Dimitrov began unfurling his majestic single-hander. One he unleashed down the line at the start of the third set would have made Federer himself purr - sadly the great man was off court at the time, no doubt tucking into afternoon tea.

The man who began the grass court season with two Tour-level wins in his life has forgotten how to lose

As Fery went an early break down in the fourth set the scoreboard looked imposing. But having come back from 4-1 down in both the fourth and fifth sets of his third-round win over Zizou Bergs, Fery was not about to panic.

He broke back; Dimitrov broke again; Fery broke back again. At 4-5, 0-40 on the Dimitrov serve Fery had three points to take it into a fifth set. On the third he hammered a backhand past Dimitrov at the net and launched into a wild, fist-pumping jig of delight.

The fifth set was fearfully tight - even Federer was leaning forward in his chair, in tune with the tension of the match. At 4-4 and again at 5-5, Fery extracted himself from sticky situations.

And so to a match tiebreak - first to 10 points - Fery's second in a row here. He opened it with only his fifth ace of the match and went 4-2 up with a punched backhand return and a rush to the net - the modern equivalent of the Henman chip and charge. Dimitrov won three points in a row, then double faulted.

Another wonderful volley combination from Fery made it 6-6. Then another ace. Dimitrov went wide and Fery led 8-7 - win two points on his serve and he was home. He dug a backhand deep into the corner and Dimitrov sliced into the net - how often had we seen that play pattern?

A Dimitrov return into the net and Centre Court erupted in noise. It may not be the Azteca but when Fery needed it most, this grand old arena roared him home.

Sports.title: All hell will break loose at the World Cup... if the shameful truth about FIFA's Team USA decision ever gets out: GAVIN NEWSHAM
Sports.content:
Three weeks into the FIFA World Cup and, predictably, it's become less about the players and more about the man who seems determined to make every tournament his own: FIFA President Gianni Infantino.

It's not just that TV cameras appear to find Infantino at every opportunity, cutting to him in the stands almost as often as they do the action on the pitch. Increasingly, there's a perception that his influence stretches far beyond the VIP box and into the game itself.

That perception only intensified on Thursday when USA striker Folarin Balogun was sent off after accidentally catching Bosnia and Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemovic on the ankle during the Americans' Round of 32 victory.

The dismissal carried an automatic one-match suspension, ruling out one of the USMNT's biggest attacking threats for Monday night's blockbuster last-16 showdown with Belgium in Seattle. Balogun, 25, has already scored three goals at this World Cup and losing him appeared to be a major blow to USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino's hopes of keeping America's dream alive.

With no mechanism for overturning a red card once it has been issued during the tournament, it appeared that Pochettino would be forced into a major tactical rethink for the biggest game of the competition so far.

Then came an intervention that changed the entire conversation.

President Donald Trump became involved in the situation, and reports suggested that a call from the President to Infantino played a decisive role in the suspension of Balogun's ban, clearing the way for the attacker to feature against Belgium.

'Thank you to FIFA for doing what was right, and reversing a great injustice,' Trump wrote on Truth Social following the decision.

The FIFA World Cup has become less about the players and more about the man who seems determined to make every tournament his own: FIFA President Gianni Infantino

USA striker Folarin Balogun was sent off after accidentally catching Bosnia and Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemovic on the ankle during the Americans' Round of 32 victory

President Donald Trump became involved in the situation, and reports suggested that a call from the President to Infantino (l) played a decisive role in the suspension of Balogun's ban following the player's scuffle with Muharemovic

For USMNT supporters, it was a moment of relief and celebration.

For many other soccer fans across the football world, it was something else entirely, a decision that raised serious questions about consistency, process and the integrity of disciplinary rules at the highest level.

Belgium, predictably, appealed the ruling, though the chances of another FIFA reversal were about even with Switzerland winning it all. The request was rejected just hours before kickoff on Monday.

Just watch what happens when Balogun scores the go-ahead goal. All hell will break loose. Perhaps that's most damaging of all, the impression this flippancy creates.

But should anyone really be surprised by how this has played out?

After all, FIFA — and Gianni Infantino — has long faced scrutiny over the way disciplinary processes are interpreted, applied, or occasionally bent, especially when high-profile names are involved.

One example frequently cited is the case of Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo, who was shown a red card for violent conduct against the Republic of Ireland in November 2025. Under standard procedure, that dismissal would typically have carried a three-match suspension, potentially ruling him out of Portugal's opening World Cup fixture against the Democratic Republic of Congo in Houston on June 17.

However, Ronaldo ultimately avoided serving the full suspension after FIFA's disciplinary structures intervened and applied Article 17 of the organization's code — a rarely used provision that allows for sanctions to be adjusted in exceptional circumstances.

Donald Trump took to Truth Social on Sunday morning to praise FIFA for 'doing what was right'

Belgium is now, predictably, appealing the ruling that overturned Balogun's suspension (Pictured) Belgium head coach Rudi Garcia (left) with goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois (right) in Seattle

Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo, was shown a red card for violent conduct against the Republic of Ireland in November 2025; Ronaldo ultimately avoided serving the full suspension

At the time, the decision was already controversial in some quarters of the game.

Now, in the context of the Balogun case, it has resurfaced as part of a wider debate about consistency and transparency at the very top of world football. And it is that wider pattern, or at least the perception of it, that will concern soccer fans: the sense that, in modern FIFA, no decision ever feels entirely beyond influence.

Besides, it's hugely hypocritical too.

Ever since he became president of FIFA 2016, Infantino has been at pains to say how politics shouldn't have any place in soccer, despite regularly turning up at the Oval Office or attending event like the Summit for Peace held in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt in October 2025, alongside 20 world leaders.

So don't blame Donald Trump for getting this red card overturned – blame Gianni Infantino.

It's his endless grandstanding and courting of the President that has led directly to this.

Since Trump returned to office, Infantino has spent extraordinary time and energy cozying up to the President, even creating a new 'FIFA Peace Prize' which Trump accepted just weeks before green-lighting military attacks on Venezuela and, more recently, Iran.

Even former FIFA boss Sepp Blatter, a man mired in controversy and corruption allegations during his 17-year tenure as president, took to social media to voice his concerns.

'If a US President intervenes with the FIFA President — and a player is suddenly cleared before a World Cup knockout match — the question is unavoidable: Quo vadis, FIFA?,' he posted.

'Football must never become a playground for political power.'

But that ship, in my opinion, has long since sailed.

FIFA has a long history of sidestepping political controversy – remember the corruption clouds over the World Cups in Russia 2018 or the human rights protests at Qatar 2022?

This time, though, there is no hiding – especially for Infantino.

Don't blame Donald Trump for getting this red card overturned – blame Gianni Infantino (Pictured: Infantino and Trump in June)

By appearing to kowtow to Trump, Infantino may have thought it guaranteed FIFA a smooth and successful World Cup but it's a decision that will come back to bite him and FIFA.

And it's only going to get worse.

What if it happens again? What if the USMNT lose to a controversial goal against Belgium in this evening? Will the Donald Trump and the White House be on the FIFA hotline again?

The noble thing, of course, would be for Mauricio Pochettino to leave Balogun out of the match against Belgium but that won't be happen, not when he's the USMNT's biggest goal threats.

But power corrupts, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.

No doubt, American soccer fans are jubilant, and not only for having their star player back, but for recognizing that their country finally understands how the beautiful game is played – off the field.

Whether or not Infantino directly influenced the decision to overturn Balogun's red card, the perception that FIFA's president holds enough sway to shape disciplinary outcomes is deeply damaging, especially when all it appears to have taken was a phone call from the White House.

Football depends on trust in its institutions, and when that trust is eroded, the game's integrity suffers.

For the good of the sport, Infantino should step aside before confidence in FIFA is lost altogether.

Sports.title: Buckle up AC Milan fans! Grinning Ruben Amorim jets in to Italy to begin his new gig at San Siro - as ex-Man United boss claims he has a BIGGER job on his hands than at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Buckle up AC Milan fans! Grinning Ruben Amorim jets in to Italy to begin his new gig at San Siro - as ex-Man United boss claims he has a BIGGER job on his hands than at Old Trafford

How much is David Beckham set to pocket from his World Cup brand deals? Take on our quiz in our newsletter HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

AC Milan's new era under Ruben Amorim is underway but their new head coach has come with a stark warning.

Amorim was appointed as AC Milan's new boss last month, signing a three-year contract.

The Portuguese jetted into Linate Airport in Milan on Monday and was a picture of delight as he prepares to begin work at the Italian giants.

And while speaking to reporters, he made a comparison of the task in hand to his ill-fated spell at Manchester United.

Amorim was sacked as Red Devils head coach in January - just 14 months after taking the reins there.

During his time at Old Trafford, the 41-year-old bemoaned of the 'storm coming'. And while excited to begin his new job in Italy, he's warned San Siro supporters to expect some tough times ahead too.

Ruben Amorim arrived in Milan on Monday as he prepares to begin life as AC Milan head coach

Amorim told reporters that this job will be bigger than the one he had at Manchester United

The 41-year-old was sacked as United head coach in January after an ill-fated 14 months there

'I'm really very happy to be here, it's an honour to be the coach of Milan,' he's quoted by Calciomercato as saying.

'Why did I choose Milan? If you read an old interview of mine you will understand it, for me a special club.

'It's a very big challenge that I accepted even if after the last one [at Manchester United] I told myself to accept a smaller one.

'Perhaps it is a greater challenge than the last. I'm proud to be here, we all are, me and my staff.'

Amorim replaced Massimiliano Allegri who was sacked at the end of the season after Milan failed to secure a top-four spot and qualify for the Champions League in 2026-27.

AC finished 17 points behind bitter rivals Inter Milan who won Serie A, but despite that gap - Amorim insists he is here to bring success back to the Rossoneri.

'I'm at Milan to win, if you're Milan coach you have to have this mentality,' he added.

'I'm not naive, I know there's a lot of work to do, but if you're the Milan coach you have to play to win.'

Sports.title: Folarin Balogun STARTS for United States despite Belgium legal threat after Donald Trump call
Sports.content:
Folarin Balogun STARTS for United States despite Belgium legal threat after Donald Trump call

The USA take on Belgium in the last-16 of the World Cup but the game has been marred by controversy with Folarin Balgoun in the starting XI having seen a ban overturned by FIFA

View 2 Images Folarin Balogun has been named in the USA starting XI vs Belgium (Image: Getty Images)

Folarin Balogun has controversially been named in the USA's staring XI for their World Cup clash with Belgium. The forward was initially suspended for the game following a red card that he was awarded against Bosnia & Herzegovina.

‌



But it was then announced that Balogun's ban had been suspended for a year following a review by a FIFA Disciplinary Committee. It was just the second time that a red card had ever been overturned in a World Cup.

‌



That has seen criticism directed at FIFA from all quarters, with UEFA expressing their “disbelief” and saying that the overturn was was “unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable”. Meanwhile, the Belgian FA said that it would contest the eligibility of Balogun's place in the game, after previously stating that they were 'deeply concerned' by the situation.

‌



Balogun was also hit with a $40,000 (£29.8k) fine by FIFA for his red card despite the decision to overturn it. Half of that fine is payable by the US Soccer Federation.

Regardless, USA boss Mauricio Pochettino has handed Balogun a place in the starting XI against Belgium. The forward will be hoping to add to the three goals that he has scored at the tournament so far.

The decision comes after a lengthy statement from FIFA President Gianni Infantino explaining the conversation he had with US President Donald Trump regarding Balogun's ban.

‌



Belgium to make last-ditch Folarin Balogun challenge after FIFA throw out legal appeal READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino breaks silence on Folarin Balogun decision after Donald Trump bombshell READ MORE :

He wrote: “I have seen the public comments regarding the decision of the independent FIFA Disciplinary Committee related to the suspension of Folarin Balogun, and I would like to reiterate a fundamental principle of FIFA’s governance.

“FIFA’s judicial bodies are independent. They operate autonomously, apply the FIFA Disciplinary Code, and decide cases based on the applicable regulations and the specific facts before them. Their independence is essential to the credibility and integrity of football, and this must always be respected.

“Yes, I regularly discuss matters related to the FIFA World Cup with the President of the United States, and on this matter, I did receive a call from President Donald Trump, just as I receive calls from heads of state, government officials, football stakeholders and business executives from around the world on many different issues.

‌



View 2 Images Balogun was sent off in the clash against Bosnia & Herzegovina (Image: Getty Images)

“During our conversation, I explained that there was an ongoing legal process involving FIFA’s independent judicial bodies and that the case would be decided in due course by the competent bodies. That is how FIFA’s system works, and it is a principle that I will always uphold.

“I read the decisions of the FIFA Disciplinary Committee when they are issued. Sometimes I am surprised by them. Sometimes I agree with them, and sometimes I disagree.

‌



“What I always do, however, is respect those decisions and the autonomy of the bodies that make them. Whether we personally like a decision or not is irrelevant.

“Respect for independent institutions and the rule of law is what protects the integrity of our competitions and the credibility of FIFA at all times.”

Sports.title: Wimbledon Royal Box guests desert Roger Federer in sad scenes
Sports.content:
Wimbledon Royal Box guests desert Roger Federer in sad scenes

Tennis icon Roger Federer was left on his own in the Wimbledon Royal Box

View 2 Images Roger Federer sat on his own in the Wimbledon Royal Box. (Image: BBC)

Roger Federer cut a lonely figure as the sole occupant pictured in the Wimbledon Royal Box on Monday. The Swiss tennis legend, who has claimed victory at SW19 on eight occasions, returned to the iconic venue where he is regarded as a legendary presence, not merely for his on-court achievements, but also for the tremendous affection he receives from the crowds.

‌



That warmth, however, did not appear to stretch to his fellow Royal Box guests, as Federer was spotted sitting in splendid isolation without a single familiar face beside him.

‌



He was in attendance for Alexander Zverev's clash against Jiri Lehecka, his third match of the day watched from the finest seat in the house on Centre Court.

‌



Federer had already taken in Jasmine Paolini's victory over Alex Eala on the same court during Monday's opening match.

He stayed put as emerging British talent Arthur Fery announced himself on the world stage with a breathtaking five-set win over Grigor Dimitrov, during which the victor gave him a special mention.

Arthur Fery in sweary moment at Wimbledon as star put on the spot over comments READ MORE :

Clare Balding cut off by Tim Henman after Arthur Fery stuns Wimbledon READ MORE :

Yet after nearly four hours of Fery's gruelling battle with Dimitrov, which ended 7-5 3-6 4-6 6-4 7-6(7) in favour of the home favourite, the Royal Box guests made a swift mass departure.

‌



They filed back inside in considerable numbers, presumably to grab a bite to eat or take a well-earned break between matches.

But when Zverev and Lehecka strode out onto court to contest a place in the quarter-finals, the BBC could only pick out Federer remaining in the stands.

Federer will undoubtedly be thrilled at being singled out by Fery, who pointed to the 44-year-old up in the then-packed stand, and said: "First time on this court. Five sets against an absolute legend of the game. I grew up five minutes from here. We've got probably the greatest of all time in the front row watching. I saw him."

‌



View 2 Images Roger Federer was honoured in the Royal Box earlier on Monday. (Image: Getty)

Speaking before the match, the Brit revealed that watching Federer compete on the very same court had driven him to pursue a career as a professional player.

"I've watched matches on Centre Court before," the British No. 3 explained last week. "I watched the final in 2014, I think Djokovic-Federer. That's my main memory of watching a big match there.

Article continues below

" I would go down there and have a look around. We're used to playing in front of a lot of people in big stadiums. And Centre Court is probably the most famous tennis court in the world. I've played on other big courts, so I'm a bit... I'm not used to it, but I've had experiences on big courts before."

Sports.title: Arthur Fery in sweary moment at Wimbledon as star put on the spot over comments
Sports.content:
Arthur Fery in sweary moment at Wimbledon as star put on the spot over comments

Arthur Fery overcame the odds to defeat Grigor Dimitrov in a five-set thriller on Centre Court at Wimbledon

View 3 Images Arthur Fery has impressed at Wimbledon (Image: James Fearn)

Arthur Fery vowed not to swear on microphone after the BBC confirmed they would not be repeating what he had shouted to his box following his remarkable Wimbledon victory over Grigor Dimitrov. Fery defied expectations on Centre Court, recovering from two sets to one and a break down to shock his experienced rival.

‌



The wildcard struggled to find words when interviewed on court by Rishi Persad, who acknowledged the Beeb would not be broadcasting exactly what he had said moments after securing the win.

‌



"I'm not going to swear. That would be a problem," Fery said with a smile, in apparent acknowledgement of those comments.

‌



"But yeah, first time on this court, five sets against an absolute legend of the game. I grew up five minutes from here, I grew up coming to watch matches on this court. We've got probably the greatest of all time watching in the front row. I saw him. And now playing here in front of all you guys, having the support and winning. It's unbelievable."

Fery, 23, knew before the opening point that this already represented his finest ever Grand Slam performance. He defeated Damir Dzumhur, Otto Virtanen and Zizou Bergs - the latter in a gruelling five-setter - to earn the showdown with fellow wild card Dimitrov.

Arthur Fery wins again as last Brit standing defies odds to reach Wimbledon quarter-finals READ MORE :

After claiming the opening set via a tie-break, the Brit dropped the following two and might have worried the fairytale was ending. However, as his 35-year-old opponent fatigued, Fery managed to take the fourth and force a deciding set.

‌



A 10-point tie-break felt like the only way to settle matters in the fifth set, and so it turned out to be. The duo exchanged early mini-breaks in a tense battle before Fery kept his composure to triumph 7-5, 3-6, 4-6, 6-4, 7-6.

View 3 Images Arthur Fery won a five-set epic against Grigor Dimitrov (Image: BBC)

The Brit was quizzed on how he managed to pull off yet another remarkable comeback from the edge of defeat. "It's been the story of the tournament for me," he replied.

‌



"I was really close to losing my last round as well and again today, a break down in the fourth. Just trying to keep fighting, keep having a good attitude, committing to what I'm trying to do on the court and it managed to pay off. I'm playing really well with my back against the wall and again it paid off today."

View 3 Images Fery was in dreamland after his victory (Image: Getty)

Reflecting on the emotion and drama of the occasion, he added: "I couldn't have imagined it. A week ago I would have been happy to win a few matches here and now winning four matches, being in the quarters, it's a dream of mine."

Article continues below

Fery will next face Flavio Cobolli in the quarter-finals after the No. 9 seed defeated Alex de Minaur earlier on Monday. The young Brit has already got the better of the Italian at a Grand Slam this year, sending him packing at the Australian Open.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo suffers heartbreak in final World Cup game as Spain win late vs Portugal
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo suffers heartbreak in final World Cup game as Spain win late vs Portugal

PORTUGAL 0-1 SPAIN: Mikel Merino plundered a dramatic additional time winner for Spain to ensure Luis de la Fuente's side advance to the World Cup quarter-finals

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo was left heartbroken following Portugal's late loss to Spain (Image: Alex Slitz)

Cristiano Ronaldo's dream of winning the World Cup went up in smoke as Spain's Mikel Merino struck in the dying embers of their Round of 16 match to break Portugal hearts.

‌



All eyes were on Ronaldo and Portugal in Texas after the multi-time Ballon d'Or winner, 41, confirmed this would be his final appearance at a World Cup finals.

‌



And Ronaldo's final attempt to conquer the world ended with a whimper rather than a bang as Portugal were beaten late by Spain in a match that will not live long in the memory.

‌



Merino popped up at the death with a slick finish to set up a frantic finale as Portugal desperately tried to find the goal that would keep their World Cup dream alive.

Cristiano Ronaldo breaks down in tears as World Cup dream over after late Spain winner READ MORE :

Cristiano Ronaldo confirms 2026 World Cup will be his last for Portugal READ MORE :

But those final few minutes were a stark contrast to the hour and a half that had preceded it.

For more than an hour, it felt as though it would take more than the regulation 90 minutes for a conclusion to come.

‌



Spain enjoyed the lions' share of possession and the better chances but were unable to translate that into a goal, while Nuno Mendes rattled the crossbar for Portugal after his ferocious strike from the angle of the penalty area ricocheted off a white shirt.

Resolute Portuguese defending thwarted Dani Olmo from breaking the deadlock late in the day as Spain upped the ante in a bid to settle this in normal time.

And then it was Merino who popped up in the 91st minute to eliminate Portugal and Ronaldo. It certainly wasn't the type of performance that supporters have become accustomed to from Spain - they were certainly made the battle and fight for their victory.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Merino celebrates his winning goal against Portugal (Image: Getty Images)

That's exactly what they did and when the moment came for them to be clinical, they were. Merino, as he has done on numerous occasions for Arsenal over the past few seasons, found himself in space and fired home a brilliant finish to power his nation into the quarter-finals.

Bizarrely, it's a considerable improvement on their more recent campaigns. Since winning the World Cup in 2010, Spain have not managed to get beyond the Round of 16, even falling at the group stage in Brazil.

Article continues below

And while they've not secured their spot in the last eight in style, not many of a Spanish persuasion will care all that much.

Sports.title: Clare Balding cut off by Tim Henman after Arthur Fery stuns Wimbledon
Sports.content:
Clare Balding cut off by Tim Henman after Arthur Fery stuns Wimbledon

Tim Henman and Clare Balding were discussing Arthur Fery's victory over Grigor Dimitrov live on the BBC

View 3 Images Clare Balding, Tim Henman and Jamie Murray were discussing Arthur Fery's win (Image: BBC)

Tim Henman swiftly intervened during the BBC's post-match discussion of Arthur Fery's victory over Grigor Dimitrov. The British wildcard secured his spot in the quarter-finals with a dramatic fifth-set tiebreak, setting up a clash with Flavio Caballo.

‌



Balding noted that Fery turns 24 on Sunday, which happens to fall on men's finals day, suggesting he could potentially go all the way.

‌



"It's his birthday on Sunday Tim! Men's finals day," the BBC presenter remarked. Pundit Jamie Murray responded: "It's written in the stars."

‌



Balding went on: "And 25 years ago today, so before he was born, the only wildcard to win Wimbledon, Goran Ivanisevic, did that. I mean.."

But Henman was quick to steer the discussion away from that particular memory, cutting in: "This is a much better story, let's not go back to 2001!"

Arthur Fery wins again as last Brit standing defies odds to reach Wimbledon quarter-finals READ MORE :

Balding quickly changed tack, conceding: "OK, let's just keep looking forward, you're right." Croatian star Ivanisevic had defeated Henman in a thrilling five-set semi-final before claiming the title. It marked the third of Henman's four semi-final defeats at the Championships.

‌



Meanwhile, Murray believes Fery will enter his quarter-final meeting with the No. 9 seed as a considerable underdog.

View 3 Images Arthur Fery is a Wimbledon quarter-finalist (Image: Getty)

He said: "He would still start the match as underdog given the difference in ranking and experience, and Cobolli having just coming off the final at Roland Garros, but I think Arthur has proven to be a great grass court player and poses a lot of different questions to players.

‌



"He's not afraid to come forward, he's approached the net more than anybody in this tournament. He asks different questions, asks players to come up with passing shots at regularity and Cobolli will have to be on guard at being rushed.

View 3 Images Tim Henman shut down Clare Balding (Image: BBC)

"Arthur likes to take time away from his opponents - not necessarily through pure power in his game and in his shots, but more in his court awareness, court craft, coming forward, seeing his opponents off balance and rushing the net, ghosting in, crush and rush on the return, but also the ability to build his points.

Article continues below

"But he's also quick to see his opponents off balance and he uses that opportunity to move forward and finish the point at the net."

Sports.title: Keir Starmer stepped in to stop FIFA moving England's World Cup kick-off over Mexico altitude fears
Sports.content:
Keir Starmer stepped in to stop FIFA moving England's World Cup kick-off over Mexico altitude fears

The UK Government stepped in to oppose FIFA moving the England vs Mexico match from 1am, fearing Thomas Tuchel's side would have less time to adapt to the altitude for their Round of 16 clash

View 2 Images England beat Mexico in Mexico City (Image: Richard Pelham, Getty Images)

Keir Starmer stepped in to stop FIFA from bringing forward kick-off at the Estadio Azteca, over fears the alteration could hand World Cup co-hosts Mexico an unfair edge over England.

‌



The UK Government intervened through diplomatic means to block moving the fixture from 1am to 7pm BST because it would mean Thomas Tuchel's squad had less time to acclimatise to the altitude, it is understood. Starmer ordered the intervention after being made aware of the potential issue by the Football Association, which is understood to have contacted Downing Street ahead of the match.

‌



England battled past hostility, altitude and Jarell Quansah's red card to clinch a thrilling 3-2 victory against Mexico on Monday morning UK time and secure a quarter-final showdown with Norway.

‌



View 2 Images Starmer stepped in over fears Mexico would get an unfair advantage by moving the kick-off time (Image: DAN KITWOOD, POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino breaks silence on Folarin Balogun decision after Donald Trump bombshell READ MORE :

Trump admits not knowing what a red card was before Balogun sending off as Ted Cruz thanks him for FIFA call READ MORE :

The fixture was scheduled to kick-off at 1am UK time (6pm local time), but with the risk of lightning in the vicinity, the stadium implemented its thunderstorm protocol and the game eventually began at 2am UK time (7pm local time).

‌



Outgoing Prime Minister Starmer intervened last week with emergency legislation to permit pubs to remain open late for the Round of 16 tie.

England went on to beat Mexico 3-2 in one of the Three Lions' most thrilling performances in recent memory. Thomas Tuchel’s belief that England can win the World Cup was fuelled by the win – but the night also increased his concerns about the potential for “erratic” officiating costing his side.

Those who stayed up late to watch the delayed last-16 encounter on an electrifying evening at the Estadio Azteca were rewarded with an inspirational performance against adversity.

Article continues below

England overcame hostility, altitude and Jarell Quansah’s red card, among other things, to triumph 3-2 against co-hosts Mexico, with Jude Bellingham’s quickfire brace and a Harry Kane penalty complemented by dogged defending.

Tuchel’s 10 men earned a quarter-final date with Norway in Miami this Saturday and moved within three wins of joining Sir Alf Ramsey’s 1966 heroes in immortality.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel told he's 'wrong' as furious England vs Mexico referee row takes new twist
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel told he's 'wrong' as furious England vs Mexico referee row takes new twist

England boss Thomas Tuchel bemoaned the performance of the officials in the Three Lions clash against Mexico and pundit Joe Hart does not think the German coach needed to expend his energy complaining

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel was frustrated with the referee's performance (Image: Francois Nel/Getty Images)

England boss Thomas Tuchel has been told he did not need to attack the referee's performance in the Three Lions' win over Mexico. Former international goalkeeper Joe Hart said that the German coach 'got it wrong' in his post-match approach.

‌



England prevailed in trying circumstances against the tournament hosts. Tuchel's side went into enemy territory at the Azteca and endured 45 minutes down to 10 men as they secured a 3-2 victory.

‌



The former Chelsea boss twice watched VAR intervene after his team took a 2-1 lead. First, Jarell Quansah was shown a red card before Harry Kane gave away a penalty after kicking Brian Gutierrez in the box.

‌



Tuchel decried the standard of refereeing. He said: "It's just not good enough.

"The referees are just not good enough, fourth officials are just not good enough.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



Jordan Henderson shows true colours after horror England injury as World Cup plan emerges READ MORE :

Belgium to make last-ditch Folarin Balogun challenge after FIFA throw out legal appeal READ MORE :

"That's the bottom line. Three people in the VAR from South America in a match like this, if this is correct, VAR overturns... is this a clear and obvious error for the penalty? For sure not.

"They overturned a situation where he doesn't even give a foul. Referees just not good enough, fourth officials just not good enough."

But Hart, who earned 75 England caps in his career, does not believe that Tuchel's energy needed to be focused in that direction following a heroic outing from his players.

‌



View 2 Images Tuchel was furious with the officials during England's win over Mexico

"I think he has got that wrong," Hart said. "I don't know why he has gone so hard on that after such an impressive performance.

‌



"I get it, against all the odds the red card and the penalties, but I don't think they were borderline decisions. I thought they were decent decisions in the end."

Tuchel also expressed some consternation when asked about United States star Folarin Balogun seeing his one-match ban suspended for a year, having been expected to miss the game against Belgium. US President Donald Trump made a call to Gianni Infantino asking for an appeal, though the FIFA chief denies it had an impact on the outcome

"Who overturns this decision then and when? And on what grounds? How far does this go now? This is strange for me," Tuchel told reporters. “Where does this start and where does this end?"

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
